description: A script is safe to re-project to the canonical JSNode operation source form when it already has exactly one exported function with a JSDoc description, no residue declarations besides its import.meta.main command guard, that guard present, and that guard reading stdin (so canonical projection changes only the source's shape, never the command's face). An actual re-projection (projected text differs from the original) is kept only if the discoverer reads the projection back to an arguments record identical to the original's own (imports compared as a set, not by declaration order), node --check parses the written file, and, where the package's own tests can run, they pass both before and after the write. The generator's files array also carries data/records/schema/<command>.input.schema.json and .output.schema.json wherever the discoverer derived those schemas from the script's own JSDoc, relative to the script's package root, and any such schema file absent or differing from disk is applied and gated exactly like a script-text change even when the script's own text is already canonical. Any gate failure restores every touched file's exact prior bytes (removing one this run created); nothing partially applied is ever left on disk.

gates.name: round-trip-identity
gates.description: readJsnodeOperationArguments(projected text) must equal readJsnodeOperationArguments(original text) on every field except imports (compared as a set of {source, default, namespace, names} records, ignoring declaration order) and bodyText (compared with its own leading JSDoc block stripped from both sides).

gates.name: node-check
gates.description: `node --check` on the file, written with the projected text, must exit 0. A non-zero exit restores the original bytes.

gates.name: package-tests-before-and-after
gates.description: When the owning package has a test/ directory and an installed node_modules, `npm test --silent` is run in that package directory both before the write (on the original bytes) and after (on the projected bytes). A baseline that already fails is recorded and does not block the write; a baseline that passes and a post-write run that fails restores the original bytes. When tests cannot run (no test/ or no node_modules), this gate is skipped and recorded as skipped, never treated as a pass.
